driver_archetypes.rationale: Base car driver (Saval et al.). Maintained.
Car violators drawn from 'car' distribution. Maintained.
Base motorcycle driver (Saval et al.). Share reduced from 0.95 to 0.6 to allow room for early-start violators, targeting M2/early/moto (observed 0.1466) and M3/share/moto (observed 0.07615).

Moto violators drawn from 'moto' distribution. Share increased from 0.2 to 0.4 (totaling 0.6 + 0.4 = 1.0) to increase wrong-lane seeking probability (targeting M8/moto ~0.2145) and support queue_space_seeking.
Illegal left-turning motorcycles (distribution 'moto_violator'). Maintained as the sole member of 'moto_violator'.

traci_rules.rationale: Saval et al.: motorcycles at the stop line have a 50% chance to run red (observed M3/share/moto is low due to early-start stealing cases; p0=0.5 is literature baseline). k=0 (no swarm).

Target M2/early/moto (observed share 0.1466). Set probability p to match exactly. This reduces the effective red-running share for compliant motorcycles, helping align M3/share/moto and M4/overshoot_share.
Target M8/moto (observed wrong-lane share ~0.2145). Set p_wrong_lane to match exactly. This generates the observed lateral encroachment and queue-jumping behaviour.
Field observation: most motorcycles squeeze past standing U-turners. High probability (0.9) reflects this, reducing waiting time and improving M6/junction metrics.
Field observation: cars rarely bypass standing U-turners. Low probability (0.1) reflects conservative behaviour.
